verdict.rationale: Obsidian's first-party Graph view core plugin visualizes relationships between notes in the vault. Its documentation also says the graph can be filtered by a search term, which covers the core of exploring a knowledge base as a filtered graph. However, the evidence never describes the graph's interactivity (navigating, clicking, or manipulating nodes), and filtering is documented only as search-term filtering. missing for 10: explicit documentation of interactive exploration (clicking or navigating nodes, local graph), richer filter options (tags, attachments, orphans, groups), and independent hands-on corroboration of graph filtering.

support.subject: As a researcher, I can explore my knowledge base as an interactive graph of notes and connections, filtered to what I care about

citations.quote: Graph view is a core plugin that lets you visualize the relationships between the notes in your vault.
Search files lets you filter notes based on a search term.
By linking notes, you can create a network of knowledge.
